thread:
mira: Heads-up: Q3 roadmap decision needed on default on-prem packaging. Field asks split: some customers require tiny binary + customer-managed networking (air-gapped-friendly), others want turnkey distro (we manage sidecars). Need recommendation that balances install friction, upgrade UX, and SLAs.

jordan: quick summary of options?

mira: three options: 1) tiny-agent default (minimal control plane footprint), 2) turnkey-distro (includes sidecars + router), 3) staged-hybrid (agent + optional managed proxy).

kai: tiny-agent pros: simplest for firewall-heavy customers, faster security review. cons: pushes routing/health to customer, complicates fallback routing and observability. Turnkey pros: consistent telemetry + easier support, cons: larger surface area and more packaging ops.

leo: field input: two pilots demand tiny-agent for IP/egress constraints. One beta customer explicitly wants turnkey because their SRE team wants vendor-managed fallbacks.

rachel: legal/security: turnkey requires clarified KMS integration and privacy scoping; tiny-agent easier for HSM-only customers. Need to document key rotation responsibilities per mode.

mira: What about upgrades? Customers want non-disruptive upgrades and ability to move from tiny->turnkey without reinstall. Is that doable?

kai: engineering note: doable if we ship an "operator shim" that can inject sidecars post-install and update routing via CRs. Implementation work: ~3 sprints to stabilize, plus a rollback playbook. If we skip shim, migration requires maintenance window and potential IP changes.

jordan: rough cost deltas?

kai: estimate: turnkey increases packaging support effort +15% and monitoring costs +10%. Potential for slightly higher SLO exposure because we manage more components. Tiny-agent reduces our ops exposure but increases field handoffs.

mira: proposal: default to tiny-agent for GA + include operator-shim roadmap to enable turnkey opt-in. That minimizes initial surface while giving upgrade path. Also include a clear migration checklist (static IP preservation, key rotation steps, firewall rules).

jordan: agree. Action items: eng to write AD + migration cmds, product to draft pilot comms and pricing add-on, security to author KMS ownership matrix.

infra-bot: RFC created: https://intranet.redwood/rfcs/packaging-defaults-1795012345  review by 2025-08-01

kai: I'll own the AD and a PoC for the OperatorShim CRD. sample CRD:

```
apiVersion: redwood.io/v1alpha
kind: OperatorShim
metadata:
  name: add-sidecars
spec:
  enable: true
  mode: "turnkey"
```

leo: add to migration checklist: preserve external IPs, document conntrack/timeouts, include test plan for failover to cloud-hosted fallback.

mira: good. Let's sync Wed 10am PT if there are blocking disputes. Thanks all :rocket:
